verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 4 remains clean. The workflow bindings use the estate-canonical repository expression while keeping the token secret-only. The binding audit is fail-closed on missing or malformed workflow input, inventories consumers by stable structural identity, checks exact repository and token expressions, enforces repo/token pairing, and compares the live identity set in both directions against an independently maintained complete enrollment set. The hermetic tests exercise supported binding levels, quoted keys, half-bindings, whole-env deletion, both drift directions, duplicate identities, parser failures, and exact allowlist rejection without relying on crashing mutants. The live seam additionally pins the actual alert step, so moving a valid binding to the wrong step cannot satisfy the estate-wide checks. I found no remaining correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security issue in the diff.
